status: DONE -- by the registered rules: no selection design SUPPORTED (all NOT SUPPORTED); 1 vs 2 cannot be chosen on predictive grounds, so the default is 1 per rolling 24 h as a COST decision; H2-H5 hold, H1 partly. Execution-layer research, development data only, hypothesis-generating (validation wear). Nothing live, frozen or registered changed.
why: The owner asks whether the trader should be limited to 1 or 2 executed actions a day, and how a genuinely low-frequency trader should select its actions, before any Firi account is connected. No experiment has ever evaluated an EXECUTION POLICY (turnover limits, holding rules, persistence, a cost hurdle) on the development data: E001/E017 measured the BUY/HOLD/SELL signal's edge per horizon without positions or costs; E032/E033 measured direction probabilities; the 2026-11-14 replay of the owner's rule on the live record (-12.3% at 0.10% fees) was descriptive, on 56 days, in one falling market. Firi's trading fee is now verified from its official price list (0.7% on each buy and each sell, firi.com/no/priser, read 2026-11-15) and two order-book snapshots showed spreads of 1.29% and 0.98%, so a round trip costs roughly 2.4-3.2%: costs, not the cap, may decide the answer.
question: Q1: on identical development hours and identical costs, does limiting rule-1.0 to 1 or 2 executed actions per rolling 24 h (instead of 4) change its net result, and is either limit better supported? Q2: does any of four fixed low-frequency selection designs (signal persistence, a daily vote, strong scores only, a cost-aware expected-return gate) show a net advantage over cash after realistic Firi costs, in both development periods? Q3: is any policy's timing better than chance, judged against random timing with the same turnover? Q4 (descriptive): does the signal's persistence or strength change the forward 24 h / 72 h return?
duplicate_check: Not answered before. E017 (scoring 0.2.0, technical-only) found the BUY-SELL edge at 24 h +0.08% [-0.22%, +0.37%] in exploration and -0.10% [-0.49%, +0.32%] in validation, at 72 h +0.40% / -0.40%, at 168 h +0.61% / -1.08% (all intervals include zero; signs flip between periods); those are cited, not re-run. E015 tested streaks of PRICE moves (up_streak_6), not persistence of the SIGNAL. No experiment has simulated positions, turnover, risk exits or costs.

hypotheses.H1_frequency: Lower caps reduce turnover and therefore cost drag; with no demonstrated edge, A1 (1 per 24 h) loses less than A2 (2 per 24 h), which loses less than A4 (rule-1.0 as built), at every Firi cost scenario, in both periods. Measured by the paired difference of mean daily strategy returns (A1 - A2, A2 - A4), with a 95% block-bootstrap interval.
hypotheses.H2_selection: No selection design (B1-B4, at either cap) has a mean daily net return above zero (cash) with a 95% interval excluding zero under the Firi-realistic scenario (S3) in BOTH periods.
hypotheses.H3_timing: No signal-driven policy's GROSS (cost-free) final equity lies at or above the 95th percentile of its random-timing null in both periods.
hypotheses.H4_cost_gate: Under the three Firi scenarios the cost gate (B4) takes almost no position (fewer than 5 entries per year), because no signal state's estimated 24 h expected return exceeds a Firi round trip; under the low-cost reference (S1) it trades.
hypotheses.H5_persistence_descriptive: Forward 24 h and 72 h mean returns do not differ by signal run length or by score strength beyond what the intervals allow in both periods (descriptive only; never used to choose a rule here).

expectation_stated_in_advance: H1-H4 hold: nothing in 38 experiments suggests a directional edge large enough to survive a 2.4-3.2% round trip; the likely finding is that the cap matters mainly through turnover, that a correctly priced cost gate never trades at Firi's costs, and that the honest choice between 1 and 2 is a cost decision, not an edge decision. A policy that clearly beats cash after Firi costs in both periods would be surprising and is checked hardest (see tripwire).

common_mechanics.capital_and_units: Start in cash with 150 units (the owner's cap is NOK 150); cap 150; venue minimum order 10 units (Firi's minimum is unverified; it hardly binds at these sizes).
common_mechanics.decision_and_fill: One decision per saved hour, made at as_of + 1 h 13 min (the live job's time) from that hour's row only. A fill happens at that hour's close with a proportional cost c per side (fee + half-spread + slippage): a BUY of q receives q(1 - c)/close BTC; a SELL of x BTC receives x * close * (1 - c). Exactly the simulated exchange's arithmetic with fee_rate = c and slippage 0. Missing hours: no decision; positions carry. Equity is marked at closes, never with an exit cost.
common_mechanics.what_counts_as_a_trade: An executed action = one filled order (BUY or SELL), counted at its fill; a partial fill counts once. The cap is 'at most N executed NORMAL actions in any rolling 24 h' (the current implementation's window). Risk exits are executed actions that do NOT consume the allowance and are counted separately. A cycle = flat -> invested -> flat.
common_mechanics.risk_overlay: rule-1.0's, unchanged, for every A and B policy: equity more than 30% below its peak, or more than 10% below its value 24 h earlier (the row exactly 24 h earlier; none -> no daily check) -> sell everything, outside the allowance, and halt. Simulation stand-in for 'until the owner resumes': trading resumes 168 h after a halt, with the peak reset to equity. Halts are counted.
common_mechanics.sizing: rule-1.0's: size = min(f_vol, f_move); f_vol = clip(0.006 / rv_24, 0.25, 1); f_move = clip(1.5 - p, 0.5, 1); a missing input takes its minimum; confidence never used.

policies.A4: rule-1.0 exactly as built (agent/execution/strategy.py): BUY -> target min(cap, equity) * size, SELL -> 0, HOLD -> keep (trimmed to the cap); resize only when the change exceeds 20% of the cap; no reversal within 6 h; at most 4 normal actions per rolling 24 h.
policies.A2: A4 with at most 2 per rolling 24 h; nothing else changed.
policies.A1: A4 with at most 1 per rolling 24 h; nothing else changed.
policies.B1_persist_cap1, B1_persist_cap2: The hour's signal counts only after the same signal on the last 6 consecutive saved hours (a gap breaks the run); otherwise HOLD. Then A's rules without resizing (an entry is sized once; a BUY while invested is HOLD), cap 1 or 2.
policies.B2_daily_vote: Acts only on the 23:00 UTC row: the mean overall_score of that UTC day's saved rows >= +0.15 -> BUY, <= -0.15 -> SELL, otherwise HOLD; every other hour HOLD. No resizing. At most 1 a day by construction.
policies.B3_strong_cap1, B3_strong_cap2: BUY only when overall_score >= q, SELL only when <= -q, where q is the 90th percentile of |overall_score| over all EARLIER development hours (point-in-time, at least 2,000 of them); otherwise HOLD. No resizing; cap 1 or 2.
policies.B4_gate_cap1, B4_gate_cap2: State s = (signal, run-length bucket 1-5 / 6-23 / >= 24 hours). mu(s) = the mean 24 h forward return of all earlier hours in state s whose outcome was known at decision time (hours <= t - 24), at least 500 of them, else no action. From cash: BUY if mu(s) > 2c (the scenario's round trip). Invested: SELL if mu(s) < -2c. Otherwise HOLD. No resizing; cap 1 or 2. Its threshold depends on the cost scenario.
policies.C1_buy_and_hold: Buy the cap at the first hour (one entry cost), never sell, no risk overlay.
policies.C3_ma200d: A published reference rule, not a candidate: on each 23:00 UTC row, fully invested (no sizing) if the close is above the mean of the last 200 daily 23:00 closes, otherwise cash; no risk overlay.

cost_scenarios_per_side.reasons: S1 = 0.10% fee + 0.01% spread (a large venue's regular tier; NOT available to the owner on Firi; a diagnostic of gross skill under low costs). S2-S4 = Firi's official 0.70% fee + 0.10% (patient limit orders that capture most of the spread) / 0.55% (half the mean of the two measured spreads, 1.29% and 0.98%) / 0.90% (wide-spread hours). Round trips 0%, 0.22%, 1.6%, 2.5%, 3.2%. The spreads measured during this session (a public order-book sampler) are reported beside the result; the scenarios are not changed after seeing them.

metrics: Per policy x scenario x period (exploration and validation run separately, each from cash): final equity, net return and annualised return; versus cash (0) and buy-and-hold; mean daily return (UTC days) with a 95% interval; annualised Sharpe (sqrt 365); maximum drawdown; executed normal actions and risk exits; cycles; mean / median net return per cycle, win rate, average gain, average loss, profit factor; mean exposure (share of equity in BTC); mean holding time per cycle; total costs paid; halts; per calendar year return (full-range run); return in 30-day blocks classed afterwards by buy-and-hold's return (up > +10%, down < -10%, flat otherwise; descriptive only).
uncertainty: Daily returns: circular block bootstrap, blocks of 20 days, 2,000 resamples, seed 31; percentile 95% intervals, for single policies and for paired daily differences (A1 - A2, A2 - A4, A1 - A4, each policy - buy-and-hold). Random-timing null (H3): the signal-related series (signal, overall_score; run lengths recomputed) circularly shifted against prices by 200 offsets drawn uniformly from [720, N - 720] hours (seed 2038), the risk inputs rv_24 and p left aligned with prices, at S0; for A4, A2, A1, B1 x 2, B2, B3 x 2; the actual gross result's percentile among the 200. Cycle-based sample sizes: n = ((1.96 + 0.84) * sd / delta)^2 for 80% power at two-sided 5%, for delta = 0.5%, 1% and 2% net per cycle, with the time that would take at the policy's own cycle rate.

what_each_answer_means_decided_in_advanc.frequency_choice: If neither A1 nor A2 has a mean daily net return above cash with an interval excluding zero under S3 in both periods, AND neither beats its null (95th percentile) in both periods, then the data cannot choose between 1 and 2 on predictive grounds; the measurable difference is cost, and the recommended default is whichever has the lower expected cost drag under S3 (stated as a cost decision, not an edge). If exactly one of them has a positive interval under S3 in both periods and beats its null in both, it is preferred, as a hypothesis for prospective testing only. Any other pattern: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, stated as such.
what_each_answer_means_decided_in_advanc.selection_design: A design is a CANDIDATE FOR PROSPECTIVE TESTING only if, in BOTH periods: its S3 mean daily net return interval excludes zero on the positive side; its S4 point estimate is positive; its gross result is at or above the 95th percentile of its null (B4: not tested against a null; it may qualify only through the first two conditions); it has at least 20 cycles. Otherwise NOT SUPPORTED. A candidate authorises nothing by itself: the next step would be its own registration and a prospective record, with the owner's approval.
what_each_answer_means_decided_in_advanc.cost_gate: H4 holds if B4 averages fewer than 5 entries per year under S2-S4 in both periods. Then the honest reading is: priced at Firi's costs, the current signals never justify a trade.
what_each_answer_means_decided_in_advanc.persistence: Descriptive. A run-length or strength bucket whose forward-return interval excludes the period's unconditional mean in BOTH periods, with the same sign, is reported as a lead for a later registered test; nothing else is read into it.

exactness_gate_before_any_result: The research simulator is a lean re-implementation (speed: the null needs about 1,600 runs). Before any result is read, it must reproduce the production engine (agent.execution.engine.run_hour with strategy.decide and SimulatedExchange(fee_rate = c, slippage = 0); MAX_TRADES_24H set to 4, 2 and 1) for A4, A2 and A1 at every cost scenario in both periods: the identical sequence of (hour, side) actions and final equity within 1e-9 relative. And E018's predictions must reproduce its validation Brier 0.22486794688851872 to 1e-9. Either failing stops the experiment until the cause is found; nothing is changed to make it match.
tripwire: A policy with an annualised net Sharpe above 2 under S3, or a gross null percentile of 100 (above all 200 shifts) in both periods, stops the reading until its point-in-time path is checked for a leak.
stop_rules: Stop if: a gate fails; the governed reader refuses a file; the replay cache's sha256 differs; any hour after 2025-06-30 23:00 UTC is read in the development part; the implementation deviates from this record. A stopped or failed run is not re-run under a changed method as the same experiment.
validation_wear: Thirty-one experiments had examined these development periods by 2026-10-17; E001/E017 judged this exact signal on these hours. Every E038 result is HYPOTHESIS-GENERATING. Nothing here can show that a policy works; it can show that one does not, and what costs do.
compute_and_storage: Local only: no network for the development part (the live part reads the database read-only), no AI call, no new table, no workflow, no paid service. Output under research/results/E038/ (JSON + markdown, < 5 MB).
result: Simulation 2018-11-27 15:00 -> 2025-06-30 23:00 UTC; exploration to 2023-12-31, validation 2024-01-01 -> 2025-06-30; start 150 in cash each period. research/results/E038/low_frequency.json/.md. S3 (Firi realistic, 1.25% a side), validation / exploration net: A4 -93.3% / -93.4%; A2 -93.4% / -93.4%; A1 -93.2% / -95.2% (each ruined within about a year: 2019 alone -75% to -87% in the full run); B1 persistence cap1 -43.9% / -68.8%, cap2 -34.1% / -89.7%; B2 daily vote -24.8% / -31.5%; B3 strong only cap1 -3.3% / -24.2%, cap2 -3.7% / -5.3% (mean daily +0.005% [-0.146%, +0.166%] in validation); B4 cost gate 0.0% / 0.0% (never traded); buy-and-hold +149.1% / +1004.8%; cash 0; 200-day reference +21.0% / +351.2%. No B design has an S3 interval above zero in either period: all NOT SUPPORTED. Random-timing null (S0, percentile of the actual among 200 shifts), validation / exploration: A4 65 / 95.5; A2 65 / 99.0; A1 25.5 / 90.5; B1 53 / 96 (cap1), 63.5 / 97 (cap2); B2 36 / 72; B3 50 / 77.5, 52.5 / 81.5: none at or above the 95th in both periods (H3 holds). Frequency: gross turnover A4 286 / 310, A2 274 / 292, A1 201 / 215 actions a year (cap 1 removes ~30%); B1 63 / 74 vs 65 / 86; B3 34 / 41 vs 34 / 43. Paired cap1 - cap2 daily differences: A at S2 validation +0.170% [+0.070%, +0.265%]; B1 at S3 exploration +0.060% [+0.021%, +0.106%]; elsewhere intervals include zero (A at S3 validation +0.003% [-0.152%, +0.143%], the accounts being ruined alike). By the registered frequency rule: neither A1 nor A2 is positive at S3 or beats its null in both periods, so the data cannot choose on predictive grounds; cap 1 has the lower turnover in every comparison, so the default is 1 per rolling 24 h, as a cost decision. H1 partly (lower caps trade less; a clear difference only at S2 validation). Cost gate (H4 holds): its estimated 24 h return at the end of development was +0.75% for BUY runs >= 24 h and +0.71% for SELL runs >= 24 h, below +0.25% elsewhere; never above a Firi round trip (1.6%-3.2%), so 0 entries at S3/S4 and about 1 a year at S2 in exploration. Persistence (descriptive, H5 holds): in exploration, runs >= 24 h preceded HIGHER 24 h returns for BUY (+0.63% [+0.21%, +1.07%]) AND SELL (+0.64% [+0.10%, +1.22%]) and runs of 1-5 h lower ones; none repeats in validation (every interval includes zero): no directional lead. Sample sizes (S3 validation, selective designs): per-cycle SD 5.5%-11.6%; +1% net per cycle needs 240-1,060 cycles, 8-66 years at their cycle rates. Live record (descriptive only, 2026-09-19 -> 2026-11-15, 1,355 hours, BTC about -19%), S3: A4 -36.0%, A2 -33.9%, A1 -29.3%, B1 -17.0%, B2 -11.5%, B3 -10.3%, B4 0.0%, buy-and-hold -20.2%; signal 3.7 changes a day, median run 3 h, as in development.
